clue.text: Proposed action is to have coppers slightly reduced at the Yard

indicators.note: a word cut down only slightly loses just its final letter here

parts.note: coppers is slang for the police

explanation.surface: Someone proposes trimming police numbers at Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly reduced' takes the last letter E off POLICE, leaving POLIC; Scotland Yard in the surface is just Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy is a course of conduct an organisation proposes to follow.

clue.text: Exercise to make suppers dissipate

indicators.note: to dissipate is to scatter, so the letters of the word before are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A workout routine meant to burn off one's evening meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms.

clue.text: Officer turning up, superior male who fills in for someone else?

definitions.text: who fills in for someone else?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer
U stands for upper-class, superior

explanation.surface: An officer arrives, and a lofty man stands in for an absent colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or priest temporarily standing in for another.

clue.text: A word disguised in tricky code for 'timber'

indicators.note: being disguised inside a tricky cipher means the letters are mixed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A word is concealed in a cunning cipher standing for timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised in tricky' scrambles the letters of A WORD and CODE together; 'code' is fodder, not a cipher hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedarwood is the fragrant wood of the cedar tree, a kind of timber.

clue.text: Pigheaded old boy taking one day going about old city

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a date is one particular day
Ur is the ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A stubborn former pupil spends a day touring an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just joins the old boy to the rest; Ur is the ancient Sumerian city of Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Financial record enables cheat to be found out

indicators.note: found out hints at being worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Company accounts let a fraudster be exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance sheet is a statement of a firm's assets and liabilities at a date.

clue.text: Set adrift female members of the family as' unwanted'

indicators.note: unwanted letters are removed from the word

parts.note: aunties are female relatives
the word as, taken as written

explanation.surface: Female relatives are cast off as unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwanted' removes A and S from AUNTIES; the stray quote marks are print artefacts.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a boat is to release it from its moorings, setting it adrift.

clue.text: Imitator admits purpose desire ultimately to be successful candidate?

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an ape is one who imitates
point means purpose, as in what's the point

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A copycat has a purposeful wish to land the job.
explanation.walkthrough: APE admits POINT plus E, the last letter of 'desire'.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointee is the person given a post, the candidate who succeeded.

clue.text: Monarch was on throne, maybe the last character to be seen as' inferior'

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
sat means was seated, as on a throne
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A ruler on the throne may be regarded as second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals that Z is an example of a last character; quote marks are print artefacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes a poor substitute, an inferior imitation.

clue.text: English shilling, copper (old penny)-old money still used somewhere

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
D stood for the old British penny, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A list of old British coins, with a currency still in use elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money used S for shilling and D for penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was Portugal's currency and remains the currency of Cape Verde.

clue.text: Animal to frolic quietly with us over time

indicators.note: over here means placed across the top of, enclosing the letter

parts.note: to play is to frolic
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A creature playing silently alongside us for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is a duck-billed egg-laying mammal of Australia.

clue.text: Individual beginning to wangle everything in smart delaying tactic

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside another

parts.note: smart means a sharp pain, a sting
one means a single individual

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: One person schemes cleverly to stall proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is obstructing by refusing to answer or by delay.

clue.text: Ruin facing one taken in by Devil-good helper needed

indicators.note: taken in by means enclosed within the following word

parts.note: Satan is the Devil
to mar is to spoil or ruin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Facing ruin after being deceived by the Devil, one needs a kind rescuer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' puts ruin in front of one; 'needed' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samaritan, after the parable, is a kind stranger who helps someone in need.

clue.text: Turn out, being enthralled by the victory

indicators.note: being enthralled by means held captive inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Ousted, yet captivated by the triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel tenants from a property.

clue.text: Maybe she fixes decrees

parts.note: she is an example of a pronoun
cements means fixes firmly

explanation.surface: A woman perhaps settles official orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe she' asks for the class of word 'she' belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronouncements are formal declarations, like decrees.

clue.text: Football team had to adapt

parts.note: Orient is Leyton Orient, a London football club
had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: A football club needed to adjust.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club, often just called Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate oneself is to adjust to new surroundings.

clue.text: Retired boxer perhaps who gives an explanation

parts.note: ex means former, retired
a boxer pounds opponents, so is a pounder

explanation.surface: A former fighter now explains things.
explanation.definitionFit: An expounder sets out and explains a doctrine or idea.

clue.text: Pop shows drew in devious spectators who'd avoid paying

indicators.note: devious means winding or twisting, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pop concerts attracted crafty onlookers who wouldn't buy tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Window-shoppers look at goods in displays with no intention to buy.

clue.text: Pets perhaps to increase walking pace?

parts.note: the clue word pets is what you get when step is rearranged, with out as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: Pet animals urged to walk faster.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards as a clue: STEP OUT would be wordplay for 'pets', OUT signalling an anagram of STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To step out is to walk briskly, lengthening one's stride.

clue.text: Have a drink outside shed that's locked?

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around the next piece

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a hut is a shed

explanation.surface: Drinking outside a shed that is padlocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut up means closed and locked, as a house shut up for winter.

clue.text: Back university person adhering to a faith

parts.note: hind means rear, at the back

explanation.surface: A returning student who follows a religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, a faith of India.

clue.text: University favourite collects second-he's this having expected a first?

definitions.text: he's this having expected a first?

indicators.note: collects means gathers in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A university favourite student gets a second-class degree when a first was expected.
explanation.walkthrough: A first and a second are UK degree classes; getting a second when expecting a first would upset anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset means distressed, as one would be after a disappointing result.

clue.text: See sugar lose value after crash

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters before are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sugar prices plummet after a market crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Laevulose is fructose, the sugar found in fruit and honey.

clue.text: Music-maker making arrangements for one to sing out

indicators.note: out means removed, taking those letters away

parts.note: organising means making arrangements
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choir director organises things so that someone can sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes I and SING from the end of ORGANISING.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a keyboard instrument that makes music.

clue.text: A thousand involved in travel broadcast

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside the next piece

parts.note: transit is travel from place to place
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Travel coverage broadcast to a thousand listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to send out a signal, as radio broadcasts do.

clue.text: Girl and US soldier love being leisurely

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
GI is a US soldier
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl and an American soldier take their time in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical term for a slow, unhurried tempo.

clue.text: After quiet period of relaxation I start to gain energy for standing

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a rest is a period of relaxation

indicators.note: start to points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: After a quiet break, I begin to build up my strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is high status or reputation in others' eyes.

clue.text: Former Chancellor taking the sword to tax initially

parts.note: brand is an old poetic word for a sword

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before

explanation.surface: An ex-finance minister wields a sword against taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy Brandt was West German Chancellor; the surface hints at a British Chancellor of the Exchequer.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Brandt led West Germany as Chancellor from 1969 to 1974.
